Session context dump for T532 (prescription deletion, Ruling 9).

## (1) Hypotheses formed and ruled out

**Scope of 'prescription': whole file vs Prescriptions section.** Considered treating cadence steps and the operator-ruling section as prescriptions too. Ruled out for cadence (it is an ordering, not a set of independently-enforceable rules) and for the operator-ruling section (dated operator text, deliberately formatted as 'prohibitions with the observed failures attached'; only its stale-reference first sentence was touched, and only because the bullet it pointed at was deleted).

**'Route each message by its reader' as not-yet-enforced.** First classified it as behavioral (nothing refuses a wrongly-routed message). Overturned: the brief's bar is 'the enforcing command exists', and managent tell / inbox --ack / sync orchestrator (T352) are exactly the mechanism the prose said did not exist ('the human ... is the only mechanism there is'). Leaving known-false prose would violate the brief's own honesty rationale for keeping unenforced prose.

**Table row per deleted prescription vs merged rows.** Merged the two managent-audit WARN rows (untracked held source; stale bin/managent) into one row listing both prescriptions -- the brief requires every deleted prescription listed, not one row each.

## (2) Hazards, smells, fragile assumptions

**The shrink bar nearly failed.** First draft: 94 -> 99 lines, -251 bytes, because verbose table rows plus header syntax outweigh single-line bullets. Fix: terse rows (the ruling itself says the command's message is the detail), merged audit rows, unwrapped two cadence steps, deleted the superseded delegate-the-thinking bullet. Anyone repeating a ruling-9 pass should budget for table-syntax overhead: 2 header lines + 1 intro against every deletion.

**Enforcement is a spectrum and the table flattens it.** purge/done/claim REFUSE; audit only WARNS; the pre-commit holder guard covers only unlabelled commits touching held paths. The table marks each row 'refuses'/'warns'/'gates' to keep the distinction, but a reader could over-trust a WARN-level row.

**Line-number refs in the findings file are commit-relative.** main.zig line refs (1996, 2058, 2740, 3114, 7144, 7265, 7377) were read at working tree state 0d3f43e-dirty; they will drift.

## (3) Uncertainties in deliverable

**'Course rev 3' ruling text not independently read.** The brief quotes Ruling 9; I executed against the brief's statement of it and did not locate the Course rev 3 document itself.

**managent standing 'auto-registers' verified by code presence (cmdStanding, auto-registered bundle body at main.zig ~7910) and help text, not by a live run** -- running it would write the live kanban from a leaf seat.

**Verb-glossary trim in the Commands section** is ruling-9-shaped (prose duplicating what the commands and spec.md carry) but the glossary was documentation, not strictly a prescription; it is not a table row, it is disclosed in the findings notes instead. If the Orchestrator judges that out of remit, the revert is one hunk.

## (4) Things that misled or cost time

**Estimating shrink by eye.** Two rounds of byte arithmetic on ~200-char wrapped lines were both wrong; wc before/after on the working tree was the only reliable measure. Measure first, edit second.

**orient principle 5 vs bundle deliverables.** The bundle declares only findings/T532-prescription-deletion.json; orient principle 5 requires a second file, findings/<id>-context.json (this file). Written to satisfy the principle; managent done checks only the bundle's list, so the discrepancy is invisible to the gate.
